text: Assume for contradiction that the square root of 2 equals p/q with p and q integers and q not zero
Recall the rational root theorem for polynomials with integer coefficients
Recall the fundamental theorem of arithmetic: every integer has a unique prime factorisation
Compute the decimal expansion of the square root of 2 to many digits
Note that 1.4 squared is less than 2 and 1.5 squared is more than 2
A contradiction follows from assuming the square root of 2 is p/q in lowest terms
The equation x squared minus 2 equals 0 has no rational roots
In p squared = 2 q squared, the prime 2 appears an even number of times on the left and an odd number of times on the right
There is no smallest positive integer q for which q times the square root of 2 is an integer
